newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chadian president denies human rights abuses.
newsitem.headline: Chadian president denies human rights abuses.

text.p: Chadian President Idriss Deby said in an interview published on Wednesday there were no political prisoners and no press censorship in his country.
He accused Amnesty International of lying about his human rights record.

"In contrast to those who preceded me, my reign is not based on human rights violations, but on the democratic process," Deby said in an interview in the weekly magazine Jeune Afrique published as he arrived in France for a five-day official visit.
He said reports by Amnesty International citing human rights abuses in Chad were mostly lies.
"I am not saying that everything is false in Amnesty International reports. They contain 20 percent truth and 80 percent lies, statements that are gross fabrications," he said.
"In Chad there are neither political prisoners nor press censorship," he said. "I am the guarantor of respect for human rights in Chad. I am answerable only to the Chadian people."
A June 1996 report by Amnesty International included Chad in a list of countries where cases of torture and ill-treatment were reported.

"Hundreds of people died apparently as a result of torture in custody or from inhuman or degrading prison conditions in 14 countries including Chad, Guinea, Kenya, Rwanda, Senegal and Sudan," it said.

Deby said he saw no risk of Chad's army staging a mutiny like that in the Central African Republic or Congo because he was planning to raise the salaries of soldiers, who he admitted have been underpaid for more than 20 years.
"It's an injustice, I would even say a tragedy because it's as if these men were not Chadian like the rest of us, as if they had fewer rights but more duties," Deby said.
"I will personally see to it that these inequalities are reduced, and the military knows it very well. They know that a mutiny never resolved anything."
Deby was scheduled to meet French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on Thursday.
